import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "source0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_0.csv",
    "source1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_1.csv",
    "source2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_2.csv",
    "source3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_3.csv",
    "source4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_4.csv",
    "source5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_5.csv",
    "source6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_6.csv",
    "source7": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_7.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source0"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source1"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source2"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Inducted By']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source3"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Spotify']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source4"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Influenced']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source5"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Certified Units (Millions)']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source6"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Times on Cover of RS']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source7"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Score']

# Step 2: Merge all source tables on 'Artist' using left joins progressively
# Start from df2 because it has the most target columns and is likely the "dimension" table
merged = df2.copy()

# Merge df0: Albums in RS500
merged = merged.merge(df0, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df1: Top 100 Singles, Highest Position
merged = merged.merge(df1, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df3: Spotify
merged = merged.merge(df3, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df4: Influenced
merged = merged.merge(df4, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df5: Certified Units (Millions)
merged = merged.merge(df5, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df6: Times on Cover of RS
merged = merged.merge(df6, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge df7: Score
merged = merged.merge(df7, on="Artist", how="left")

# Step 3: Ensure all target columns exist in the merged dataframe
# Target columns and their types:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': integer,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Inducted By': string,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float,
#  'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer,
#  'Highest Position': integer,
#  'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float,
#  'Spotify': integer]

# Step 4: Data type conversions and filling missing values where appropriate

# Convert columns to correct types, handling missing values:
# For integer columns, fill NaN with 0 and convert to int
int_columns = [
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Influenced",
    "Albums in RS500",
    "Top 100 Singles",
    "Highest Position",
    "Times on Cover of RS",
    "Spotify",
]

for col in int_columns:
    if col in merged.columns:
        merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    else:
        # If column missing, create with default 0
        merged[col] = 0

# For float columns, fill NaN with 0.0 and convert to float
float_columns = ["Certified Units (Millions)", "Score"]
for col in float_columns:
    if col in merged.columns:
        merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0.0).astype(float)
    else:
        merged[col] = 0.0

# For string columns, fill NaN with empty string
string_columns = ["Artist", "Inducted By"]
for col in string_columns:
    if col in merged.columns:
        merged[col] = merged[col].fillna("").astype(str)
    else:
        merged[col] = ""

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    "Artist",
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Inducted By",
    "Influenced",
    "Certified Units (Millions)",
    "Albums in RS500",
    "Top 100 Singles",
    "Highest Position",
    "Times on Cover of RS",
    "Score",
    "Spotify",
]

merged = merged[target_columns]

# Step 6: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/target_multisource_cot.csv"
merged.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/training_7.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all tables on 'Artist' using inner joins to keep only artists present in the main dimension table (source2)
df = source2.merge(source4, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source5, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source0, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source1, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source6, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source7, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source3, on="Artist", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns that appear to uniquely identify rows in target examples
# These are: Artist (string), Year Inducted (int), Years Waited (int), # of Years Nominated (int), Inducted By (string)
# Aggregate all other columns by sum (since the target examples have fewer rows than joined data)
group_cols = ["Artist", "Year Inducted", "Years Waited", "# of Years Nominated", "Inducted By"]

agg_dict = {
    "Influenced": "sum",
    "Certified Units (Millions)": "sum",
    "Albums in RS500": "sum",
    "Top 100 Singles": "sum",
    "Highest Position": "sum",
    "Times on Cover of RS": "sum",
    "Score": "sum",
    "Spotify": "sum"
}

result = df.groupby(group_cols, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Ensure column order matches target schema exactly
result = result[[
    "Artist",
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Inducted By",
    "Influenced",
    "Certified Units (Millions)",
    "Albums in RS500",
    "Top 100 Singles",
    "Highest Position",
    "Times on Cover of RS",
    "Score",
    "Spotify"
]]

# Write the final output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_35/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
